articles.title: 全球首个乙肝功能性治愈新药在中国获批上市
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，国家药品监督管理局官网显示，批准贝普若韦生（英文名：Bepirovirsen；商品名：贺舒可）上市。该药品联合核苷（酸）类似物（NAs）用于慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染的功能性治愈。近日，国家药品监督管理局通过优先审评审批程序，批准 GlaxoSmithKline Trading Services Limited 申报的 1 类创新药贝普若韦生钠注射液（商品名称：贺舒可）上市，该药品联合核苷（酸）类似物（NAs）用于慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染的功能性治愈，适用于以下人群：已接受 NAs 治疗至少 6 个月、HBV DNA<90 IU / mL、HBsAg≤3000IU / mL、无肝硬化的慢性乙型肝炎病毒感染成人患者。IT之家查询获悉，贝普若韦生已于今年相继在日本、美国、加拿大获批，成为全球首个且唯一获得多国监管共同认定、以“功能性治愈”为治疗目标的乙肝新药。在中国，该药的商业化由正大天晴承接。2026 年 5 月 11 日，中国生物制药宣布附属公司正大天晴与 GSK 达成独家战略合作，正大天晴负责贝普若韦生在中国内地的进口、分销、医院准入及推广活动，该产品产生的全部销售收入确认为正大天晴营业收入；GSK 继续作为药品上市许可持有人（MAH），负责监管注册、质量控制与药物警戒等。双方初始合作期为 5.5 年，期满后可协商延长。此次在华获批，是基于 B-Well 1 和 B-Well 2 两项 III 期研究的积极结果。这两项研究旨在评估贝普若韦生功能性治愈慢乙肝患者的有效性和安全性。其中，中国亚组数据显示，经核苷（酸）类似物治疗、病毒已获抑制的患者接受 24 周贝普若韦生治疗后，基线 HBsAg 不超过 3000IU / ml 的患者，功能性治愈率达到了 24%；而基线 HBsAg 不超过 1000IU / ml 的患者，功能性治愈率达到了 35%。

articles.title: 设计时速 350 公里：安徽巢马、淮蚌、淮阜高铁明日集中开通运营
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，上铁集团今日宣布，11 月 27 日，安徽巢湖至马鞍山高铁（简称巢马高铁）、淮北至蚌埠高铁（简称淮蚌高铁）、淮北至阜阳高铁（简称淮阜高铁）将集中开通运营，车票自 11 月 26 日 19 时 30 分起对外发售。IT之家附三条高铁介绍如下：巢马高铁巢马高铁西起巢湖东站，向东经马鞍山市含山县、和县、当涂县、经开区等地，东至马鞍山东站，新建正线全长约 61 公里，设计时速 350 公里。沿线设巢湖东、含山、郑蒲港、马鞍山南、马鞍山东 5 座车站，其中含山、郑蒲港、马鞍山南为新建车站，其余为既有车站。全线设有桥梁 24 座、隧道 6 座，桥隧比达 79.6%。开通运营初期，铁路部门每日安排开行图定动车组列车 8 列，均为跨线动车组列车。马鞍山东站、郑蒲港站、含山站至合肥站最快 1 小时 7 分钟、47 分钟、34 分钟可达，打通马鞍山至省会合肥高铁直达通道。淮蚌高铁淮蚌高铁北起淮北北站，向南经淮北、宿州、蚌埠三市接入蚌埠南站，新建正线全长约 161 公里，设计时速 350 公里。沿线设淮北北、淮北西、宿州西、双堆集、固镇南、蚌埠南 6 座车站，其中淮北西、宿州西、双堆集、固镇南为新建车站，其余为既有车站。全线设有桥梁 23 座、隧道 1 座，桥隧比达 89.9%。开通运营初期，铁路部门每日安排开行图定动车组列车 46 列，均为跨线动车组列车，从淮北西站、宿州西站出发可直达上海、浙江、江苏、皖南皖中等地区多个城市。淮北西站至南京南站、上海虹桥站、杭州西站最快 1 小时 37 分钟、3 小时 6 分钟、4 小时 3 分钟可达，宿州西站至南京南站、上海虹桥站、杭州西站最快 1 小时 21 分钟、2 小时 49 分钟、3 小时 46 分钟可达，固镇南站、宿州西站、淮北西站至合肥站最快 57 分钟、1 小时 9 分钟、1 小时 26 分钟可达；结束淮北向南高铁出行绕行徐州的历史，径路进一步优化。淮阜高铁淮阜高铁东起淮蚌高铁双堆集站，经亳州市蒙城县、利辛县、阜阳市颍泉区接入阜阳西站，新建正线全长约 142.5 公里，设计时速 350 公里。沿线设蒙城、利辛、颍泉北、阜阳西 4 座车站，其中蒙城、利辛、颍泉北为新建车站，阜阳西为扩建既有车站。全线设有桥梁 14 座，桥梁占比达 88.98%。开通运营初期，铁路部门每日安排开行图定动车组列车 18 列，均为跨线动车组列车。利辛站、蒙城站至合肥站最快 1 小时 26 分钟、1 小时 15 分钟可达；阜阳西站、利辛站、蒙城站至淮北西站最快 1 小时 13 分钟、52 分钟、37 分钟可达，阜阳西站、利辛站、蒙城站至蚌埠南站最快 1 小时 11 分钟、50 分钟、35 分钟可达。

articles.title: 阿维塔 T09 旗舰 SUV 亮相华为乾崑生态大会，将于明日广州车展中国首秀
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日现场消息，阿维塔 T09 旗舰 SUV 今晚亮相华为乾崑生态大会，该车将于明日 10:20-10:40 在广州车展迎来中国首秀。据IT之家此前报道，今年 10 月 12 日，阿维塔 T09 概念版迎来全球首秀。新车作为阿维塔与华为乾崑联合设计的首款高端旗舰车型，设计灵感源于 VISION XPECTRA，配备四激光雷达。新车采用全新设计语言，晶钻阵列大灯搭配雕塑格栅，拥有“绛红”与“棉白”双拼车色；全新的 D 柱发光徽标与整体架构融为一体，车尾则配备修长的一体式晶钻尾灯。新车内饰也迎来焕新升级，采用全新 Vortex 情感涡流设计，配备三联屏，互动屏幕向外拓展延伸至车门一体化布局，拓宽视觉边界的同时，也能让驾驶者可以用更好的视角看清信息。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，香港运输署宣布，香港网约车车辆驾驶许可证将于 11 月 30 日上午 10 时起接受当地民众申请，符合资格的申请人届时可通过香港政府一站通网站提交网上申请。此次驾驶许可证不设发放数量上限，全年开放申请，并非采取先到先得的方式。根据相关规定，申请人除了满足多项法定条件外，还必须通过的士及网约车综合笔试，并完成网约车司机职前培训课程。已经持有有效的士驾驶执照的人士则可获豁免，无须重新参加综合笔试或修读网约车司机职前培训课程，可直接向运输署申请驾驶许可证。符合资格的人士从 11 月 30 日上午 10 时起，可随时通过香港政府一站通网站提交网上申请，整个流程均采用电子化方式。成功获批的申请人将收到电子版驾驶许可证。香港运输署特别提醒，由于网约车驾驶许可证没有发放数量限制，且全年接受申请，因此并非先到先得，申请人无须急于在下周一开放申请后第一时间提交材料。至于网约车车辆许可证，运输署计划于 2027 年年初公开接受申请。根据法例规定，车辆许可证的发放数量上限为 1 万张。如果收到的有效申请数量超过法定上限，运输署将通过抽签方式分配。IT 之家小伙伴记得用最会买打车，享受折扣价的同时还可以获得返利，单单都能省钱！

articles.title: Ask HN: What's your minimum criteria for a project to be low-AI or not vibecoded
articles.content:
Let's assume we want to have a monthly thread for projects that are not vibe-coded or no/low-AI.Of course this filter cannot be actually enforced, and maybe very few projects are totally without any use of AI (even research could count as AI use). But if devs want to give a honest indication of the level of AI use, what do you think are good criteria for this?It is an interesting question to ponder. We could have a spectrum of AI use based on the following:- Is the project based on a one-shot prompt (perhaps followed by subsequent prompts), with no look at the code?- Are the tests and/or specs human-written and maintained?- Has AI been used to write any part of the code at all?- Has the dev actually written any part of the code by hand? What estimated percentage.- Is pretty much each edit reviewed/approved by the dev, only PRs? Is there any dev review at all?What do you think is a good criteria to consider a project an AI work, or a human work with AI assistance?

articles.title: 宾利首款纯电车型 Torcal 发光格栅细节公布：76 颗钻石元件 +202 颗 LED
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，宾利公布了 Torcal 发光格栅的细节，该车是宾利首款纯电车型。前格栅由 76 个独立加工成型的钻石形元件组成。夜间，超过 26 万个激光钻孔的微孔以及藏在表面之下的 202 颗 LED 会让整个设计亮起来。IT之家注意到，夺目的格栅之外，还搭配了一套全新的大灯方案，配备 Micro LED 投影模块，可对光束进行更精确的控制。这套新灯组在克鲁（Crewe）设计完成，对宾利最具辨识度的设计特征之一作出了全新的诠释。车头一直是宾利最具辨识度的部分之一。Torcal 在此基础上继续延伸，从欧陆 T（Continental T）的格栅中汲取灵感，同时赋予其彻底的现代演绎。最终呈现的是一种立体设计，由 76 颗大小不一的水晶状钻石组成，每一颗都由手工单独装配。每个钻石形元件都由独立的透明罩保护，该罩所用材料与涂层与大灯相同。白天，格栅看上去像是一块经过雕塑的金属表面；而当夜幕降临，整个总成便会亮起，让 Torcal 拥有极具辨识度的发光前脸标识。细节上的讲究也延伸到格栅周围的金属边框。边框上有超过 26 万个细小的激光钻孔，下方布置了 202 颗 LED，使光线均匀分布于整个表面。灯光关闭时，边框仍保持传统金属格栅的外观。宾利还对这款格栅进行了大量耐久性测试，包括耐磨测试和碎石冲击测试，以确保它能经受日常使用。此外，一套主动式冷凝管理系统有助于让透明罩长期保持通透。买家可以在两种格栅版本中选择，其中包括亮饰套装（Bright Pack），配有金属质感罩盖的钻石形元件。宾利汽车设计总监罗宾 · 佩奇（Robin Page）阐述了这一新设计背后的思路：“我们并不是单纯想做一个发光格栅。我们的目标是打造宾利下一个标志性的面孔。从品牌传承中汲取灵感，我们把精致的钻石工艺与先进的照明技术结合起来，为 Torcal 创造出独具一格的新身份 —— 无论白天还是夜晚，都一眼就是宾利。”Torcal 的新照明技术并不局限于格栅。每个大灯集成四个灯光模块，其中包括两个各含 16,000 像素的垂直 Micro LED 投影模块，以及用于近光和远光的常规模块。据宾利介绍，该系统的照明强度足以让人在 1 公里的距离外阅读书籍。两个 Micro LED 投影模块分工不同。上方单元覆盖 40 度角范围，照亮驾驶员视野的边缘，这在过弯时尤为有用，有助于改善弯道内侧的可见度。下方投影模块的光束更窄，为 20 度，能够把光线更精确地聚焦到需要的地方。该系统还能自适应调整光线分布，在改善驾驶员视野的同时减少对其他道路使用者的眩光。配合发光格栅，新大灯让宾利 Torcal 在夜间拥有独特的外观。

articles.title: 消息称育碧正大力推动将生成式 AI 深度融入游戏开发流程，项目若未引入 AI 需申报原因
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，据外媒 Vertical Slice 报道，育碧正在大力推动生成式 AI 深度融入游戏开发流程，如今公司团队在提交新游戏项目提案时，必须说明生成式 AI 能够如何帮助开发游戏，如果团队不打算使用生成式 AI，则需要向公司高层明确解释原因。多名员工透露，如果某个游戏项目提案没有涉及生成式 AI，同时给予高管的理由不能够让人信服，就很难获得批准。还有匿名员工表示：“公司告诉我们，使用 AI 能够提高小型、精简且灵活的团队提交项目提案的速度。管理层希望团队能够快速推进、反复迭代，并及时放弃不合适的项目，从而筛选出真正有潜力的创意。”过去一年多以来，育碧一直在进行大规模业务重组，包括成立新的子公司、将旗下《刺客信条》《孤岛惊魂》《彩虹六号》等主要游戏品牌整合至不同的创意部门，同时关闭部分工作室，并经历了多轮裁员。一名员工对此表示，育碧目前陷入了由管理层自上而下推动的“AI 狂热噩梦”，公司内部士气本就不高，而首席执行官 Yves Guillemot 已经将公司的未来押注在这项技术上，并要求其他员工跟随这一方向。

articles.title: 《GTA 6》耗电实测：电视开 HDR 竟比主机还费电
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，想在罪恶都市（Vice City）充分享受视觉盛宴？你可能得多掏一点电费。德国能源供应商 Rabot Energy 测算出了在四款主机上分别游玩 80 小时《GTA 6》所需的电费，并揭示了电视开启 HDR 模式会让电费增加多少。《侠盗猎车手 VI》（Grand Theft Auto VI）自 11 月 19 日发售以来，数百万玩家已花费大量时间探索虚构的莱奥尼达州。德国能源供应商 Rabot Energy 发布了一份分析，把现有的硬件功耗实测数据与游戏发售周末（11 月 19 日至 22 日）记录的德国电价结合起来。若在傍晚时段游玩 80 小时，搭配 55 英寸电视的 Xbox Series S 是最省钱的组合，电费为 5.82 欧元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 42.5 元人民币）。Xbox Series X 以 8.32 欧元（现汇率约合 60.8 元人民币）紧随其后，PlayStation 5 与 PS5 Pro 在关闭 HDR 的情况下分别为 10.52 欧元（现汇率约合 76.9 元人民币）和 11.06 欧元（现汇率约合 80.8 元人民币）。耗电大户并非主机，而是处于 HDR 模式的电视，其功耗甚至可能超过主机本身。Rabot 以两款 55 英寸、120 Hz 电视作为参考显示设备：TCL 55C7K Mini-LED 和 LG OLED C5。这两款电视的 HDR 额定耗电量均高于 Xbox Series X 的游戏功耗预估值。在 SDR 模式下，两款电视的功耗约为 76 瓦；开启 HDR 后，LG OLED C5 的额定耗电量升至 191 瓦，TCL 55C7K 则达到 242 瓦。Rabot 在成本估算中采用了较低的 LG OLED C5 的 HDR 功耗数据。在测试 PS5 与电视的组合时，Rabot 发现，改用能效更高的那台电视（LG）并开启 HDR，会使 PS5 整套设备的耗电量从 23.3 千瓦时升至 32.5 千瓦时，账单因此多出 4.16 欧元（现汇率约合 30.4 元人民币）。相比之下，在开启 HDR 的情况下把 80 小时游戏时间全部从傍晚挪到深夜，也只能省下 1.55 欧元（现汇率约合 11.3 元人民币）。需要说明的是，这些都是基于德国电价的估算结果。为省下几十元钱，你会关掉 HDR 吗？

articles.title: 东风着陆场准备就绪，迎接神舟二十三号飞船返回
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 26 日消息，据央视新闻报道，今天，东风着陆场组织所有搜救力量，展开神舟二十三号载人飞船返回前的全系统综合演练，做好迎接航天员回家的准备。参加此次演练的搜救回收力量包括地面分队指挥车、搜索车、通信车、医监医救车等车辆装备以及空中分队 5 架直升机。演练中，空中分队根据落点坐标通报，精准降落在返回舱周围，实现“舱落机临”。据了解，神舟二十三号载人飞船预计着陆时间为凌晨时段（具体时间未公布），针对夜间低温条件，医疗救护队备好睡袋、盖毯等御寒物资，对医监医保车进行维护，确保车内温度适宜。考虑到本次乘组中有外籍航天员和女航天员，医监医保环节在通用流程之外，进一步细化了个体化健康评估和护理照料方案。从出舱协助、车载监测到生活饮食，各环节均提前确认，确保保障措施符合每位航天员的身体情况和个人习惯。目前，地面分队已对着陆场区进行了全面勘察，规划出多条应急通行路线，东风着陆场搜救装备完成性能调试，通信链路实现全时段覆盖，东风着陆场各搜救力量准备就绪，装备设备状态良好，气象条件满足任务要求，具备执行返回任务条件。据IT之家此前报道，神舟二十三号返回段将由航天驾驶员张志远担任指令长。返回乘组包括神舟二十三号乘组的张志远与黎家盈，以及完成短期联合飞行任务的巴基斯坦航天员穆罕默德 · 齐尚 · 阿里。

articles.title: Marc Levinson on How UPS Created Modern Logistics
articles.content: UPS was founded nearly a century ago in the basement of a Seattle saloon by James E. Casey and his business partner Claude Ryan. It is now hard to imagine modern, globalized life, and the logistics required to prop it up, without the innovations Casey and his partners at UPS cooked up during the company's early decades. Marc Levinson has just written a biography of Casey and the company he founded — UPS Man: James E. Casey and the Creation of Modern Logistics — which was a lot harder to do than you might imagine, because Casey shunned the spotlight and his contributions were virtually unknown outside of UPS. In today's episode, Levinson tells us why UPS is so secretive about its history, how Casey and his partners helped figure out the last mile problem and popularized parcel delivery, and how scientific management theories influenced everything the company did. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Irreducible Governance Structure for Autonomous Agent Systems: Fair Allocation, Strategy-Proofness, and Multi-Scale Composition
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31284v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous agent governance is commonly framed as a problem of enforcing correct execution. However, in multi-agent systems, an equally fundamental question precedes execution: which agents are allowed to act.
  In this paper, we show that allocation is not an auxiliary concern but a structural component of governance. When multiple agents compete for execution under constrained resources, any allocation mechanism introduces unavoidable trade-offs between fairness, efficiency, and resistance to strategic manipulation. We formalize this through a set of impossibility results, including Sybil amplification and the incompatibility of desirable allocation properties.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31301v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio-video (AV) deepfakes can fake the face, the voice, or both. Most benchmarks only ask whether a clip is real or fake, so they cannot show whether a detector relies on the picture, the voice, or encoding traces. We present MOZAIC, a paired benchmark with a 4-way label in which every source clip is released in all four combinations of real or fake video and real or fake audio so each modality contribution can be measured directly. Fakes cover inner-face swapping, whole-frame video diffusion and voice conversion. MOZAIC has 137,745 clips from 15,014 source pairs and four tasks: T1 AV authenticity, T2 manipulation type, T3 identity verification and T4 explanation. We evaluate 12 AV multimodal LLMs (MLLMs), train four detectors and fine-tune MLLMs with LoRA. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31329v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Attribute reduction in incomplete information systems is difficult because missing values break the equivalence-class structure of rough set theory. We propose the Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Set (COFRS) model. Each object is described by its set of present attributes. The similarity of two objects is a weighted overlap on the attributes present in both, divided by the fixed number of attributes |A| instead of the size of their union, so missing values are penalised globally and are not matched as wildcards. From this similarity we define a soft dependency degree based on weighted granule consistency, and we search for reducts by greedy backward elimination in O(|U|^2 |A|^2) time. We show that the relation is symmetric and non-reflexive, that the dependency degree is not monotone, and we give a sufficient condition under which monotonicity holds. articles.content:

Abstract: In recent years, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved significant progress in chart-to-code generation. Unlike static chart-to-code generation, which emphasizes visual consistency, interactive chart-to-code evaluation targets behavioral consistency, requiring chart states to evolve correctly under sequences of user interactions, thereby rendering traditional one-step evaluation paradigms ineffective. articles.content:

Abstract: Recent advances in MLLMs have improved social understanding, enabling models to recognize emotions and distinguish truthful from deceptive behaviors. However, existing benchmarks largely focus on coarse-grained emotion recognition or binary truth-deception detection, overlooking the diverse ways people manipulate information in conversations, such as withholding, leakage, fabrication, evasion, and defensive counterclaim. Understanding these behaviors requires reasoning about underlying facts, participant knowledge, and conversational context, making them difficult to evaluate reliably. To address this gap, we introduce InfoCon, a multimodal benchmark for fine-grained information manipulation in conversations. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31424v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As LLMs become more capable, agents can perform more complex tasks with tools and maintain longer interactions with users. These benign conversations contain evidence on task results, user concerns, and operational constraints. The risk is that attackers who can observe benign conversations (evidence) may construct stronger indirect prompt injections without increasing the attackers' control over prior turns or the later injection. However, we still lack a clear study of how effectively attackers can select and use this evidence. To address this gap, we introduce ContextLure, a red-teaming framework in which an attacker silently observes an existing benign conversation, extracts evidence, and constructs an injection. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31427v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents operate through harnesses that define system prompts, action formats, feedback loops, and resource constraints. A model may possess the knowledge needed to solve a task yet fail to express that knowledge through a particular harness. This raises a basic question: when a policy fails under a given harness, is it missing task knowledge or the competence to operate the interface? We distinguish two components of agentic competence: task competence, the knowledge and reasoning needed to solve a task, and interface competence, the ability to act on that knowledge through a given harness. articles.title: Taxi: Analyzing Agents at (Real) Scale
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31457v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this technical report, we present Taxi -- a system for debugging, clustering, and monitoring agents at scale. Taxi scales to millions of steps efficiently. This is made possible by a combination of scalable analysis methods. Taxi relies primarily on clustering to generate a taxonomy over steps for a structured overview of the data, and provides full SQL access for engineers and automated agents to ask complex questions. Clustering and querying are best used together in a hybrid pipeline guided by a coding agent. Taxi also includes an experimental integration of Jev-style decision models: models that map state and bounded questions directly to typed, probabilistic decisions. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31475v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spatial reasoning agents increasingly rely on external tools, such as 3D reconstruction, segmentation, and geometric computation, to answer questions that a multimodal large language model (MLLM) cannot resolve from pixels alone. We ask whether a frozen tool-using agent can improve its orchestration from its own interaction history, without parameter updates. Abstract: Scientific analyses that span many jobs and computing sites depend on workflow management systems to run reliably, but writing a production workflow requires expertise in such a system, which many domain scientists do not have. We wrote skills and specialist agents for the Pegasus workflow management system with a frontier model, and the PegasusAI Studio science gateway offers them to scientists through a chat interface. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31522v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: GUI agents can choose correct actions yet fail as interfaces change during deliberation. Latency alone cannot explain these failures because actions may become invalid at different interaction stages. We model four events: environment change, observation availability, decision commitment, and action receipt (EODA). Our accelerator-resident GUI controller, Chronotope, maintains compact interaction history and selectively keeps, updates, or redecides pending actions. Abstract: Code-executing LLM agents submit blocks of code that issue several API writes. If a block fails after some of its writes have taken effect, the agent rewrites the block and continues. Abstract: In playtesting games, a human operator is typically required to test most gameplay elements. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31571v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autoformalization translates a natural-language statement into a formula that captures its intent, which depends on the statement's context: the background that disambiguates it. LLMs make autoformalization practical, but their probabilistic output carries no formal guarantees. We propose techniques for safe autoformalization that certify one-sided logical adequacy: a formula sufficient for the intent is safe to enforce, and a formula necessary for it is safe to rely on. We use LLMs to generate candidate formulas and order them by logical strength in an Entailment Graph (EG), an ordering a solver decides. Each edge carries a residual and a co-residual, the two adjoints of the entailment order, all fixed by the candidate pool alone. articles.title: Provably Near-Optimal PQ in the Extended Zador Model
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.31579v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper investigates Product Quantization (PQ) Optimization with Gaussian data. It offers three key contributions (i) a proof that SVD is the optimal preconditioning rotation for PQ; (ii) a new Extended Zador (EZ) estimator of the $k$-means quantization cost that is accurate in low bit rates and low dimensions; and (iii) a novel segmentation algorithm based on 1-d bin packing of global bit allocations. The result is a simple algorithm (EZPQ) with strong approximation guarantees. It matches OPQ's empirical accuracy while providing a per-instance distortion lower bound certificate under the Gaussian EZ cost model. On typical real embedding spectra, EZPQ with 2 bits per coordinate is often certifiably within 1% of the optimum in this model. It also consistently achieves a lower reconstruction error than all random-rotation-based algorithms such as EDEN, E-RaBitQ, and TurboQuant.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33163v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Offline handwritten signatures remain a primary behavioural biometric in legal and financial documents. Detecting skilled forgeries from a static raster image is hard because pen pressure, timing and stroke order are missing. This work studies a family of quantum machine learning pipelines for offline signature forgery detection on a public Kaggle corpus of images split into two classes. We pair a ZZ feature map quantum kernel with three classical learners: K-Nearest Neighbours, Support Vector Machine and Random Forest. We then propose a deeper hybrid that uses EfficientNetB0 as a frozen feature extractor, reduces the resulting 1280 dimensional representation to a qubit register sized subspace through a quantum compatible principal component projection and decides class membership with a nearest neighbour rule. articles.title: Code availability is not enough: schemas for documenting and extending data analysis
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33167v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A data analysis involves a sequence of decisions, from data cleaning to model specification, each of which can affect the reported result. Reproducing that result is not the same as understanding the sequence of decisions that produced it and the reasons for each: the code mixes those decisions with implementation details, while the manuscript states the major decisions and their rationale but scatters them across its sections and often leaves out the minor ones. A reader may then ask how the result would change under a different decision: the question itself is easy to pose, but implementing it is often non-trivial in practice. In this work, we propose a schema that represents a data analysis as a collection of decisions in natural language, from which large language models (LLMs) can generate and validate analysis scripts directly. articles.title: Temporal Exposure to Byzantine Vulnerability Under Intermittent Participation in Federated Learning
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33168v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we study the effect of participation variability on per-round Byzantine vulnerability. We formalise Dynamic Participation Exposure (DPE), a phenomenon in which the global Byzantine fraction remains below an aggregation rule's tolerance threshold, while a participating client set violates, or approaches violation of, the assumptions required for robust aggregation. Under stochastic participation, we derive the probability of per round exposure and analyse how active-set size affects the variability of the observed Byzantine fraction. We further examine the accumulation of exposure over multiple rounds and consider adversaries that selectively participate during favourable rounds. Our analysis shows that intermittent participation does not automatically imply aggregation failure. articles.content:

Abstract: Geophysical inverse problems are inherently ill-posed because of sparse observations and measurement noise. Classical sampling-based Bayesian inference methods, such as Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), are computationally prohibitive because they require many forward simulations. Data-driven machine-learning methods often struggle to produce physically consistent solutions when training data are limited. To address these issues, we propose a geophysics-informed invertible operator network (GI-ION) that integrates an invertible neural network (INN) within a deep operator-learning framework for efficient Bayesian geophysical inversion. The INN serves as the branch network and transforms the model parameters into branch coefficients that represent the forward solution and a latent variable that captures uncertainty in the inverse problem. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33179v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Traffic-related emissions are a major contributor to urban air pollution. However, existing emission models face a fundamental trade-off: macroscopic models are computationally efficient but rely on average speeds, leading to systematic errors, while microscopic models achieve high accuracy but are computationally prohibitive for large scale simulations. To bridge this gap, this study introduces Direct Emission Prediction (DEP), a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)-based deep learning model. DEP was trained on over one million synthetic trips generated by coupling real-world GNSS speed profiles with the microscopic emission model MOBSim. By processing sequential link-level inputs, including vehicle characteristics, road attributes, and ambient temperature, DEP predicts CO$_2$ and NOx emissions. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33182v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) offer an approach to identify language model representations by breaking apart polysemantic features into more sparse, interpretable ones. Yet, it is challenging to identify which of the learned features are actually stable, rather than artifacts of initialization. One approach is to train multiple SAE seeds, and compare the learned features across seeds by cosine similarity, but this is notably costly. This raises the question of whether stable features can be identified without the computational expense of training multiple seeds. In this work, we examine cross-seed feature stability across differing levels of training tokens, and demonstrate that in TopK SAEs, it is highly predictable using six computationally cheap statistics derived from a single training run. articles.title: REI: Learning Ideation from Repository Evolution
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33183v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: As AI systems become increasingly capable of executing and evaluating experiments, ideation is emerging as a bottleneck in automated scientific and engineering iteration. In many real-world domains, useful ideas are sparse and their validation is costly, making direct online exploration inefficient. We observe that repository evolution provides a scalable source of reusable technical experience: code changes record concrete technical hypotheses, while subsequent revisions, adoption, and reuse provide signals about their utility. Based on this observation, we propose REI, a Repository Evolution-driven Ideation framework that learns reusable ideation policies from repository evolution, injecting domain-specific technical experience into model parameters and reducing reliance on costly trial-and-error. Abstract: Persistent textual memory can improve LLM agents, but repeated updates can erode task performance. We ask whether memory-store statistics warn before held-out accuracy declines. These methods store trajectories, rules, workflows, strategies, or linked records, using selective retrieval or whole-store prompting. No such statistic reliably predicted early signs of task accuracy decline, and $\rho$ had zero median lead. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33236v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Full fine-tuning of large pretrained models is expensive, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) is the standard alternative. Most PEFT methods use low-rank updates, whose rank lies far below that of full fine-tuning and is the same for every input. Input-adaptive variants vary the capacity per input but remain within the low-rank bottleneck, and whether a task benefits from input conditioning is not known before training. This paper introduces Kronecker input-gated rank adaptation (KiRA). Instead of the conventional low-rank product, the update $\Delta W$ is the Kronecker product of a frozen random $p\times p$ matrix $A$ and a trainable factor $M(x)$, which overcomes the rank ceiling: because rank is multiplicative under this product, $A$ multiplies the rank of $M(x)$ by $p$ without adding trainable parameters. Abstract: The UCI Heart Disease data are a widely used machine-learning benchmark. We show that their chest-pain variable is stored in reverse of its documentation. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33249v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Dictionary methods for time series build bags of symbolic words from subsequences, but the accurate ones scale poorly. Against other families of methods, their accuracy no longer pays for their cost. We present FERRETS, a label-free dictionary transform built on WEASEL~2. It keys windows of random length and dilation into exact eight-bit words, adds a level word of each window's mean and spread, and on multivariate data adds cross-channel words. We compare it with leading classifiers, deep networks and foundation models included, on the UCR, Multiverse and MONSTER archives. FERRETS is the fastest of the eleven methods timed on UCR under a ten-thread budget. Of the ten others, only MultiRocket-Hydra is significantly more accurate, taking 24.7 times as long. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33257v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Linear attention compresses historical context into a fixed-size recurrent state, reducing the computational and memory costs of long-sequence modeling. From the perspective of test-time regression (TTR), the state matrix can be viewed as an online-learned regression model, where keys and values serve as inputs and targets respectively, and queries are used to read from the model. From this perspective, the effectiveness of state learning depends not only on the update rule but also on how the key-value learning pairs used for state updates are constructed. While existing work has largely focused on how the state is updated and organized, we investigate how the learning pairs used for state updates are constructed. Abstract: Abstract interpretation can certify properties of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), but precise analyses remain expensive. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33308v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Model merging combines fine-tuned experts into one model that serves many tasks without retraining, but merging many experts this way substantially reduces accuracy. Grouping offers a middle ground: at every layer or weight matrix, the $N$ experts are divided into $K<N$ groups, the experts in a group are merged into one shared module, and a task uses the module merged from its expert's group. Natural choices are to keep the same partners across layers or to group similar experts. Surprisingly, we find that randomly changing partners at every layer outperforms both. We call this Balanced Random Regrouping (BRR): it independently partitions the experts into $K$ equal-sized random groups at each layer (BRR-layer) or weight matrix (BRR-matrix) and merges each group with an existing method. Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) generates massive data streams, making edge computing essential for low-latency applications and 5G networks. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33332v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present an online learning system for short-term time series forecasting that enables proactive autoscaling in large-scale distributed systems. Unlike traditional forecasting methods that focus on modeling seasonality and long-term trends, the system targets high-accuracy, low-latency predictions for immediate future intervals for dynamic resource management in internet-scale infrastructures. The system employs a two-stage architecture: a seasonality decomposition stage followed by a residual correction stage using lightweight linear models with engineered features. By retraining models on-the-fly for every prediction cycle, the online prediction system continuously adapts to changing demand patterns without requiring persistent model storage or feature drift monitoring. Abstract: The Bundesrat is Germany's second legislative chamber and a constitutional veto player within its political system. The members of the Bundesrat are delegates of state governments. articles.content:

Abstract: Long-horizon Large Language Model (LLM) agents need persistent memory that surfaces the right past interaction at the right time across thousands of turns. We propose MGMem, a framework with no generative indexing calls that replaces this step with a deterministic discriminative-parser pipeline: recurring mentions across sessions are organized into an incidence graph, question mentions are resolved by a subject-conditioned three-stage resolver, and raw dialogue episodes are returned to the reader. articles.title: Psychophysics of Duration Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33176v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Studies of time perception in language models focus mainly on text-based settings. Yet multimodal models are increasingly used for tasks that require perceiving the passage of time, making the limits of their temporal perception important to understand. We measure the limits of duration perception from audio against a human baseline to address this gap. Drawing from psychophysics, we operationalise duration perception as a melody recognition task, testing when a melody becomes unrecognisable as it is slowed down. Of 21 tested models, most cannot recognise well-known melodies without labelled in-context examples. With in-context examples, seven recognise melodies reliably, most peaking within the median human recognition band. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33195v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Materials discovery is an iterative loop: experiments and calculations verify predictions, and each outcome can inform the next. Yet most predictors are specialized single-task models fixed after training. Large language models have recently emerged as predictors across heterogeneous tasks but generally underperform specialized models, and retrieval-augmented variants discard their own outcomes. Benchmarks also score queries in isolation, leaving improvement from outcomes untested. Here we construct MatMemBench, a sequential benchmark of 22 materials tasks that reveals outcomes only after prediction and tests online adaptation, memory retention and cross-task transfer. We present MatRecall, a framework that lets large language models store verified predictions, with evidence, outcome and error, as episodes and recall them without retraining. articles.title: Extraneous Cognitive Load in Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33197v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) shows that human problem-solving is affected by both intrinsic load, arising from task difficulty, and extraneous load, arising from how task information is presented. Large language models (LLMs) show analogous effects: presentation alone can affect model performance, but these effects have not yet been systematically isolated from task difficulty. To address this gap, we introduce CogLoadBench, a controlled benchmark that varies five CLT-inspired presentation factors across three reasoning task families. Across models, we find that higher extraneous load conditions often reduce accuracy by either adding competition or complicating the reasoning path. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33250v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Text embedding models can conflate surface-form similarity with factual identity. Given an altered near-copy with one corrupted fact and a differently worded fact-preserving rewrite, the base model prefers the altered near-copy. We test whether hard-negative contrastive supervision can reduce this surface-similarity shortcut. We construct FOF-Bench, an 83,263-triplet benchmark spanning five domains. Each anchor is paired with an LLM-generated, fact-preserving stylistic rewrite and a matched fact-altered near-copy. We fine-tune FOF-80M (Focus On Facts), an 80M-parameter embedding model, with a triplet contrastive objective that ranks the rewrite above the factual alteration. On 8,327 held-out test triplets, the base model chooses the factually altered text in 99.58% of cases (0.42% factual preference rate; mean separation -0.1650). Abstract: Outlet ideology is a standard explanatory variable in media framing, media effects, and political communication research, but continuous, ecosystem-wide coverage lets it enter as graded exposure rather than a coarse bin. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33307v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Decision models are language models fine-tuned to return a probability for each option of a typed query, which routers and guardrails threshold directly. They are built on multilingual bases but ranked almost entirely in English. We evaluate 25 top-ranked open-weight decision models on 17 tasks in 14 languages, comparing each language with English on parallel items. Every model loses accuracy in every language, from about 2 points in high-resource languages to 8 in Tamil, while confidence falls only half as much: a threshold set for 95\% accuracy in English yields 90% in Tamil. The size of the loss is set by the language and the base model rather than by leaderboard rank. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33327v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When users assume that an AI chatbot has mental states, they are more likely to develop over-reliance, emotional dependence, and in extreme cases, psychological harm or self-harm. However, how these mind attributions arise in conversations and how human or AI factors influence this is still unknown. We study how users attribute minds using a minimal framework: a simulated user with different characteristics chats with assistants that differ in social style and memory. We also introduce a message-level measure of who attributes a mind to whom in four directions, checked with trained coders and applied by a fine-tuned encoder that reproduces an LLM judge. Our results show that, on average, nine out of thirteen characteristics raised simulated users' attribution to the assistant. Abstract: Assistants that answer from supplied reference material often receive material that covers some parts of a user's question and not others. Existing evaluations of insufficient context mostly score one answer per question, and often treat partially sufficient context as simply insufficient. We describe a small, open evaluation that scores each part of a three-part question separately, with a verdict for parts that are answered correctly from the material but carry an added unsupported claim. On 30 cases (five scenarios, six coverage patterns, five samples each) we test claude-haiku-4-5 and llama3.1:8b. Without an explicit instruction to stay within the material, both models fill most gaps from their own knowledge (unsupported-claim rates of 0.71 and 0.90). articles.title: Open-Source FUTO Keyboard Layouts and Predictive Text for a Few Endangered Languages
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33432v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present open-source FUTO Keyboard layouts and predictive text dictionaries for five endangered Uralic languages: Erzya, Moksha, Komi-Zyrian, Livonian, and Skolt Sami. Existing Divvun Android keyboard layouts are converted automatically into the YAML format used by FUTO Keyboard. For predictive text, we construct weighted AOSP dictionaries using translated Finnish lemma frequencies together with morphological frequencies extracted from small target-language corpora using finite-state transducers. This combination provides a practical way to rank inflected word forms when large monolingual corpora are unavailable. The resulting resources offer reusable mobile keyboard support for endangered Uralic languages.

articles.content:

Abstract: Conversations are central to how people exchange information, share experiences, and develop collective understanding. Yet, across conversational settings, discussions often suffer from uneven participation, unanswered contributions, and a narrow range of perspectives. As generative AI agents increasingly participate alongside humans, hybrid human-AI conversations present a new opportunity to address these challenges. We investigate whether AI agents can serve as catalysts for human interaction, improving conversational engagement and broadening collective discourse. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33468v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A looped language model repeatedly applies the same block to its hidden state before predicting each token. The number of passes is its recurrent depth. Increasing this depth gives the model more computation per token with the same parameters. Can the shared block learn from the predictions it makes at greater depth? Following prior work, we retrofit pretrained OLMo-2-1B with a shared recurrent block and continue mid-training over varying recurrent depths. In the four-pass model, additional passes mainly redistribute probability among tokens that already rank highly after one pass. We use the continuations generated at greater depth to train only the shared block through a single pass, without reference answers or correctness filtering. We call this transfer preference write-back. Write-back further improves one-pass and multi-pass accuracy on most tasks. Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are known to misinterpret and misrepresent regional and social varieties of English other than Mainstream American English (MAE), such as African American English (AAE), yet most evaluations of these biases have relied on synthetic, stylized or decontextualized data. This paper instead evaluates LLMs on authentic, conversational AAE to more closely reflect how such models may encounter AAE when deployed as chatbots. Abstract: Language models can stand in for survey respondents, but leading approaches build their simulated people from interviews or individual records. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33510v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Detailed knowledge of a user's persona is valuable for personalizing generative AI models and agents, yet such details are difficult to obtain and change over time. We address the task of inferring persona attributes from a single day of mobile activity logs. No suitable publicly available benchmark exists for this task, so we introduce a synthetic benchmark of 1,600 persona-log pairs. We target on-device inference so that raw logs never leave the phone, which makes memory rather than speed the limiting constraint: a day of activity yields roughly 30K tokens, whose key-value cache alone exceeds the INT4 weights of a 4B-parameter model. We therefore propose a log filtering method that retains only behaviorally distinct entries. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33612v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language model agents can self-improve over time by utilizing procedural memory derived from prior task trajectories, yet the distinct utilities of memories derived from local successes and failures remain underexplored. This work studies this question in a realistic setting with heterogeneous streams of multi-domain tool-use tasks and various environment constraints common in real-world scenarios. We develop \emph{Dual-Polarity Memory with Periodic Maintenance} (DualPM), a simple, retrieval-free memory workflow characterized by (1) customizable reflection and procedural memory generation from both local successes and failures within each trajectory, and (2) periodic memory consolidation over long task streams under a given memory capacity, preventing memory explosion. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33640v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Understanding how models internally represent information is a central challenge in interpretation and control. Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose dense hidden representations into sparse features, and cross-layer methods capture structure spanning multiple layers. However, existing objectives do not explicitly train the sparse code at one layer to predict the sparse code at the next layer. We propose sparse-to-sparse feature learning (S2S), where sparse features at each intermediate layer are trained to predict those of the immediately following layer, with the final layer anchored by an output-distribution loss and optimization proceeding sequentially from output to input. Experiments across eight language models show stronger adjacent-layer correspondence than matched sparse-feature baselines. Abstract: Quality control for proposition decomposition by large language models (LLMs) raises two asymmetric questions. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33210v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for biomedical question answering, but plausible incorrect answers remain a safety risk in clinical settings. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can ground responses in medical literature, while confidence-based adaptive RAG retrieves only when the model appears uncertain. We evaluate this routing strategy on three biomedical QA benchmarks of increasing difficulty and compare models across a broad range of parameter scales. The results reveal a paradox: confidence is well calibrated (AUROC 0.78--0.89) on standard medical exam questions where retrieval adds little value (+2.4\% to -1.4\%), yet becomes \emph{near-random} (AUROC 0.506) on specialist-level questions where retrieval helps most (+11.2\%). Abstract: Alongside superposition, polysemanticity is one of the primary obstacles to achieving interpretable deep neural networks. While these phenomena are typically intrinsically linked, the Quadratic Programming Enhanced Model (QPM) naturally decouples them. Abstract: Discrete visual tokens encode images for reconstruction and serve as training targets for autoregressive image generators. A local model of the reconstruction loss yields a closest-vector problem with a decoder-dependent target and metric. Reconstruction-only search improves PSNR across the frozen tokenizers we test. Abstract: Attention over long sequences is a major computational bottleneck in video generation, which can be alleviated through sparsity and low-bit quantization. We propose JetDiffusion, a video generation system built on trainable Video Sparse Quantized Attention (VSQA), with custom inference kernels that combine native NVFP4 computation and kernel fusion. To further accelerate video generation, we combine VSQA with NVFP4 linear quantization and step distillation. Although each technique can individually preserve generation quality, jointly adapting to all three remains challenging, particularly under aggressive NVFP4 quantization. Through empirical studies, we develop an effective staged training recipe that enables stable adaptation to quantization, sparsity, and few-step denoising. Abstract: We introduce CoSMo, a compact spectral space of body motion in video, in which each motion is a single code that can be compared and edited without training, transferred to a new subject, interpolated, composed, scaled in intensity and detail, or sampled anew. Because each frequency band is the same cosine pattern in every code, codes are aligned in time, ordered from coarse to fine, and can be blended or added without matching frames. What stays constant over a clip cancels, and keeping fewer frequencies leaves less of the performer and scene. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33315v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Model merging combines multiple task-specific expert models into a single model. However, merging preserves expert capabilities unevenly across tasks. This imbalance is particularly pronounced in large-scale settings, where some tasks can suffer severe capability losses even when average accuracy remains high. To address this imbalance, we introduce Recovery-aware Task Weighting (RaTW), a model merging framework that assigns larger weights to tasks whose expert capabilities are poorly retained by an initial merged model. We quantify these recovery opportunities as the fraction of a task's labeled validation samples that its expert predicts correctly but the initial merged model gets wrong, and use the resulting task weights to re-merge the experts. articles.title: What Does RL Post-Training Teach Text-to-Image Models? A Skill-Wise Analysis of Flow-GRPO
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33316v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training has become a standard way to improve text-to-image flow models: Flow-GRPO lifts the GenEval score of SD3.5-M from 0.63 to 0.95, a gain read as the model having learned compositional generation. We ask how much of that gain the base model's own samples already contained, by measuring pass@k over shared noise seeds, one skill at a time, before and after RL, on prompts never used in training. The answer differs by skill. On four of GenEval's six skills, where 32 base samples already solve almost every prompt, the gain is sharpening: one post-trained sample is worth 4 to 10 base samples, and pass@32 barely moves. On spatial relations it is unlocking: pass@32 rises from 0.69 to 1.00, 128 base samples do not match one post-trained sample, and prompts the base model never solved in 32 samples are solved 93% of the time, as often as those it solved. articles.title: StyleID++: Position-Decoupled and Structure-Coherent Style Retrieval across Diffusion Architectures
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33323v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Attention injection offers a remarkably simple route to training-free style transfer: content queries retrieve style keys and values inside a pretrained diffusion model. We show that this operation also creates an overlooked failure mode. Position signals that are useful within one image become a spurious shared coordinate system across two spatially unrelated images, causing content tokens to favor style tokens at similar coordinates. This cross-image positional leakage appears in both convolutional U-Nets and diffusion transformers (DiTs), despite their different position mechanisms. Removing the positional shortcut exposes a second problem: unconstrained global retrieval lets related content tokens select incompatible style regions, producing fragmented appearance. articles.title: Do Not Let the Prior Heal the Anomaly: Selective Anchoring for Detection from Incomplete Measurements
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33331v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generative priors can recover anatomical detail from incomplete medical measurements, but may erase the very lesions that imaging aims to detect, even when the measurements contain evidence of them. We introduce selective anchoring that protects reliably measured image components from prior-driven changes, while allowing expressive generative models to reconstruct unresolved structure. Acquisition uncertainty in the protected components is either added deterministically to the downstream test or carried by the ensemble through stochastic perturbations of the readings. We implement this principle as a wrapper for pretrained diffusion and flow samplers and as AnchoredFM, a fast constrained flow model. Under a linear-Gaussian measurement model, the protected coefficients are unbiased in expectation and achieve nominal interval coverage across repeated acquisitions, independently of the learned prior. articles.title: Temporal Weight Surgery: Repairing Video Grounding with LLM Editors
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33339v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A surgeon first finds what is wrong, then fixes only that part. We use this idea for video grounding, where video-language models often find the right moment in a long video but write its time wrong. In Temporal Weight Surgery (TWS), a general-purpose LLM reads the model's weights and activations, finds where the error arises and repairs it there, without gradients. Separate sessions find the same cause, and this diagnosis of where and why the model fails is our main contribution. Three GPT-6 Astra sessions trace a dropped digit in TimeLens-8B to one MLP layer, and the largest edit gains 7.9 mIoU on 1,215 unseen questions and 18.3 on videos of 30 minutes or more. Two Claude Opus 5.5 sessions trace minutes written as seconds in Qwen3-VL-8B to the separator and gain 2.9 and 1.3. articles.title: LGCount: Layout-Guided Diffusion for Zero-Shot Object Counting
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33344v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Class-agnostic counting requires the user to specify what to count, usually with a class name or a few annotated boxes. We propose a richer text-based specification: a structured layout that names the target, the region that holds it, the distractors to ignore. A prompt upsampler writes this layout from the image and the requested category alone, and an image-editing diffusion model, adapted into a single-step counter, turns it into a density map. Because counting datasets pair each image with a single valid density map, a counter trained on it learns to ignore the layout. We therefore train on synthetic counterfactuals in which one image admits several valid density maps, so that the layout cannot be ignored. On FSC-147 we improve on the previous zero-shot state of the art and we set the best reported result on LOOKALIKES while being told the least about each image. articles.title: DDxBasis: Explaining Frozen Foundation Encoder-based Medical Classification by Exact Differential Diagnosis
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33358v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In differential diagnosis (DDx), a clinician explains a diagnosis by the few findings that separate it from the alternatives. Medical image classifiers cannot yet explain themselves this way. Existing explanations are either faithful but spread over hundreds of concepts, or compact but leave part of each decision unexplained. We present DDxBasis, which explains a classifier on a frozen foundation encoder as a differential diagnosis in three steps. First, a concept bottleneck reads all patch tokens at every encoder layer using gated, second-order slot attention. A concept basis then regroups the concepts into two-pole axes, each a differential between groups of diagnoses. Finally, we read a differential diagnosis from each axis through the typical presentation of its poles, the pertinent findings of the case, and counterfactual edits of borderline cases. articles.title: Searching Ultra-Long Videos with Decision Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33368v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Understanding ultra-long videos requires retrieving sparse, query-relevant evidence from extensive video histories. Existing similarity-based retrieval methods are efficient, but they encode the question and the video content independently and thus often miss evidence whose relevance requires reasoning over both. Generative large language models (LLMs) can perform such reasoning, but they typically generate text over multiple rounds of search, which makes each query slow and costly. In this work, we introduce DeLoVi (Decision Models for Long Video), a framework that leverages pretrained decision models to retrieve evidence from ultra-long videos. Like an LLM, a decision model reads the question together with the candidate evidence, so it can reason over both. Unlike an LLM, it directly outputs a relevance score without generating text, which makes it fast and inexpensive. We first present DeLoVi-S, a simple method that generates captions

articles.title: Benchmarking Segmentation Models for Scalable Mangrove Mapping with Sentinel-1/2 Imagery
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33369v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mangroves are dynamic coastal ecosystems that contribute to carbon storage, coastal protection and biodiversity conservation, but are vulnerable to climate change. Very-high-resolution imagery such as Pl\'eiades enables detailed mangrove mapping but it is costly and have a low revisit rate. Large-scale monitoring requires free and regularly available data such as Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 but their spatial resolution poses challenges for detailed mangrove mapping. In this work, we benchmark deep learning approaches for mangrove mapping from Sentinel-1 radar and Sentinel-2 optical imagery using reference maps derived from very-high-resolution Pl\'eiades imagery. We compare four segmentation configurations based on CROMA and BigEarthNet-pretrained ResNet50 representations with different segmentation decoders. We construct a mangrove mapping dataset covering French Guiana, Suriname, and Amap\'a. CROMA + UPerNet achieves the best performance

articles.title: MotifFlow: Training-Free, Self-Contained Style Transfer from Color to Motif in Rectified Flow Transformers
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33371v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Expressive style transfer must reproduce a painting's palette, brushwork, and characteristic motifs while retaining the content image's structure. Attention injection is effective in U-Net-based diffusion models, but adapting it to FLUX often transfers color without capturing the style's distinctive brushwork. Our analysis across backbones links this gap to how injected features are integrated across neighboring spatial locations. We introduce MotifFlow, a training-free, self-contained framework that combines style injection with style-alignment guidance in FLUX. Injection supplies style features during generation but does not explicitly encourage the model's native attention output to align with them. We therefore use the discrepancy between native and injected attention outputs to guide latent-space updates, encouraging the evolving image to develop the style's distinctive brushwork and motifs. articles.title: VersionGS: Compact and Motion-Robust Dynamic Gaussian Splatting via Versioned Gaussians
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33374v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent dynamic Gaussian splatting methods encode temporal change, either as smooth functions of time or as constrained updates between frames. We observe that their reconstruction quality degrades significantly under fast motion. In challenging dance sequences, their PSNR drops by 1.1-4.0 dB on high-motion frames compared to low-motion frames. To overcome this limitation, we propose VersionGS, a method that directly encodes per-frame Gaussian states and uses motion estimation only to guide reconstruction. Within each group of frames, unchanged Gaussians keep their current versions in a shared dictionary, while modified Gaussians are appended as new versions. To maximize version reuse, we introduce selective sequential construction, which refines the Gaussians selected by optical flow, photograph differences or rendering errors and leaves the others unchanged. articles.title: DreamTour: Layout Steering for Training-Free World Exploration
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33378v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Video diffusion and world models generate plausible videos but do not reliably match the requested camera direction and travel distance. We present DreamTour, a training-free framework that generates camera tours from a single image with more accurate control over camera motion. DreamTour first uses a frozen image inpainting prior to extend the photograph beyond its original field of view while preserving the input pixels. Depth-based rendering of this extended scene along the requested camera path produces approximate target views that serve as spatial guidance. We introduce Layout Steering, which aligns early video latents with these views through decaying low-frequency corrections, leaving later denoising to refine appearance and dynamics. articles.title: Effect-Driven Skill Abstractions for Offline Reinforcement Learning
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33229v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We seek to learn discrete skill abstractions to facilitate long-horizon, goal-conditioned reinforcement-learning (RL) tasks. Recent approaches have shown success by quantizing actions via clustering or reconstruction. However, these objectives lead to skills that are not directly related to what the current state affords or what the goal requires. Instead, we argue that goal-directed skills should be driven by \emph{how they affect the state} of the agent. To realize this, we introduce a novel quantization method for action chunks that optimizes next-state predictions conditioned on the current state and action. This objective encourages skills to be distinguished by the future states they lead to, resulting in a vocabulary that spans diverse outcomes reachable from a given state. articles.title: Why Does Sensor Depth Fail Learned Manipulation Policies? Finding the Failure Mode with ACT
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33352v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Learned manipulation policies, from task-specific imitation policies to vision-language-action (VLA) models, rely primarily on RGB images. While some studies report gains from sensor depth, others avoid depth cameras because of measurement noise. Depth cameras introduce both noise and missing depth values (holes), whose relative effects remain unclear. In this study, we calibrate a sensor model using a real wrist-mounted stereo camera and separately evaluate noise and holes on RGB-D imitation policies with three visual encoders in simulation. We found that complete depth improves success by approximately ten percentage points, and most of this gain persists even at twenty times the camera's noise level. In contrast, holes covering about one-sixth of the wrist image eliminate the detectable benefit of depth. articles.title: FOCI: Trajectory Optimization on Gaussian Splats for Gaussian Robots
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33380v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has recently gained popularity as a faster alternative to Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) in 3D reconstruction and view synthesis methods. Leveraging the spatial information encoded in 3DGS, this work proposes FOCI (Field Overlap Collision Integral), an algorithm that is able to optimize trajectories directly on the Gaussians themselves. FOCI leverages a novel and interpretable collision formulation for 3DGS using the notion of the overlap integral between Gaussians. The formulation presented applies to different robot morphologies (e.g., fixed and mobile base manipulators, legged robots, UAVs) and handles both static and dynamic Gaussian-Splat environments. Contrary to other approaches, which represent the robot with conservative bounding boxes that underestimate the traversability of the environment, we propose to represent the environment and the robot as Gaussian Splats. articles.title: RoboARC: Physical Puzzles for Robotic Manipulation under Spatial Constraints
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33390v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many hard manipulation tasks come down to a spatial constraint that only a few motions satisfy, such as passing a part through a gap barely wider than itself or separating two interlocked parts. These motions depend on the exact geometry of each scene, so demonstrations and skills recorded elsewhere rarely transfer. We therefore ask: when manipulation hinges on spatial constraints, can robots reason out the right motions? We introduce RoboARC, a benchmark of 90 tasks in six constraint types over rigid and soft materials, on three robots in MuJoCo. Every task is a frozen scene with a physics-based grader and a verified reference solution that replays bit-identically. Each task comes in a Privileged regime, with the full simulator state and resets, and a Standard regime with real-sensor inputs (camera images and proprioception) and a single attempt without resets. articles.title: Best-of-$N$ Test-Time Steering Can Lead to Reward Hacking in Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33398v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise for general-purpose robotic manipulation, but adapting to changing environmental conditions still remains challenging. Recent test-time steering methods have shown promise in enabling adaptive VLA policies by utilizing additional computation during deployment. In this paper, we consider best-of-$N$ test-time steering for VLA models, where multiple action candidates are sampled from a fixed policy and a verifier is used to select the best one during deployment. We show that increasing $N$ does not always improve performance when the verifier is inaccurate, and can favor candidates whose scores exploit prediction errors, a form of reward hacking. We study this effect on 60 LIBERO-Safety task-level cases using a $\pi_{0.5}$ policy, with ten repetitions per case. articles.title: An Adversarial Multi-Agent Pursuit Game for Locomotor Agility Pretraining
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33407v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agile humanoid locomotion requires controllers that can adapt to rapidly changing motion demands while remaining stable and robust. Recent locomotion controllers are typically designed with either a dense reward that is carefully shaped to encourage steps and penalize falling, or by using a reference tracking reward which teaches the controller to follow predetermined motions. Once a behavior that maximizes the reward is discovered, the controller ceases to learn. While generally stable, reference tracking methods focus on motor control separately from motion generation. Self-play has been proven as an effective technique for superhuman performance on several multiagent games like Go, Starcraft, hide-and-seek, and capture-the-flag. We train neural networks to play the game of multiagent tag in a physics simulator to study if new motion generation and control strategies can emerge through sparse feedback and competitive self-play. articles.title: OnCue: Generating Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios under Occlusion with Temporal Control
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33439v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Occluded hazards challenge autonomous driving because visibility timing determines available avoidance actions. Existing scenario generators control hazard motion without jointly specifying exposure and reference-contact times. We propose OnCue, a framework that generates safety-critical encounters in real driving logs with these temporal conditions. Scene geometry provides hidden starts and timed waypoints for pedestrian, cyclist, and vehicle trajectory generation. An offline response oracle labels encounters as Reactive (avoidable after exposure) or Anticipatory (avoidable only with earlier visibility) and stores safe maneuvers as training demonstrations. On the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, 90.1-96.6% of valid trajectories meet both requested times within +/-0.2 s. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33514v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This study investigates model predictive control (MPC) of a multirotor drone (unmanned aerial vehicle, UAV) carrying a cable-suspended payload, comparing conventional shifted initialization with Transformer-based warm starting of a sequential convex programming (SCP) optimizer. The controller uses a coupled mechanical model with an elastic cable and a double-pendulum representation of the suspended load. Its formulation includes move-blocked control inputs, finite-difference sensitivities, constrained quadratic subproblems, and input-feasibility projection. A Transformer trained on expert SCP solutions predicts an initial control sequence, which is subsequently refined by the same optimizer used for the conventional methods. Numerical experiments compare zero, shifted, and Transformer initialization under identical controller settings. articles.title: Skeptic: Grounding Failure Diagnosis for Robot Skill Discovery
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33560v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robot agents discover reusable skills by revising programs from execution feedback and retaining experience for later tasks. This process can fail when an agent treats an unsuccessful program as evidence that the task is physically impossible, ending exploration with revision budget remaining. We study this failure in Qwen3.8-27B and examine two decisions that shape skill discovery: I) how execution failures are diagnosed, and II) which lessons enter the shared skill library. Failure diagnosis requires the agent to reconstruct physical action effects from multimodal traces, while independent reproduction of a proposed repair does not require adequate task performance from its source program. We introduce Skeptic, a training-free protocol that uses measured action outcomes to guide repair and measured task success to govern skill admission. articles.title: DexEngine: Scaling Human Demonstrations into Physically Executable Whole-Robot Data
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33579v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A growing body of recent work addresses the retargeting of human hand-object demonstrations to robotic hands. To train whole-robot policies, however, the retargeted motions must be kinematically feasible and physically executable, and be produced efficiently at scale. We present DexEngine, a simulation pipeline that turns human manipulation data into train-ready, physically executable arm-hand trajectories. DexEngine first places each clip's hand-object motion where the arms can reach it, finds an arm motion that follows the human hands, and then corrects the motion in physics simulation with residual reinforcement learning. From nine human hand-object datasets, we generate about 5,200 clips for each of four dexterous hands, augmented into 65,000 trajectories (116 h) and 325,000 episodes (578 h) in total. articles.title: DFLAT: Model-based Diffusion on Differentially Flat Spaces for Long-Horizon Trajectory Optimization
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33586v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon diffusion-based planning for kinodynamically constrained systems requires both scalability and feasibility, yet existing diffusion planners typically sacrifice one for the other. We present DFLAT, a diffusion-based planning algorithm that operates directly on a differentially flat trajectory representation. Instead of diffusing over time-discretized controls, DFLAT denoises a compact set of Hermite curve parameters in the flat-output space, consisting of intermediate waypoints together with the endpoint tangents of each segment. Every denoised sample maps to a dynamically consistent trajectory, so feasibility holds by construction rather than being restored afterward. Experiments on challenging tractor-trailer planning benchmarks show that DFLAT matches or exceeds the success rates of existing baselines at consistently lower planning times, particularly on long-horizon problems requiring multiple forward-reverse maneuvers. articles.title: Greedy Decoding Hides Good Plans: Sample-and-Verify Planning for Vision-Language Driving Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33621v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly adopted for end-to-end driving planning, yet their performance is typically evaluated based on a single greedily decoded trajectory. However, greedy decoding may overlook better trajectories within the model's output distribution. Experiments on WOD-E2E and NAVSIM reveal a consistent performance gap between greedily decoded trajectories and the best sampled candidates, showing that planning errors can arise from trajectory selection, rather than trajectory generation alone. On WOD-E2E, when the ego vehicle should start moving, the model often assigns probability to different possible start times, causing greedy decoding to repeatedly favor waiting and produce a stationary plan even though moving trajectories are available. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33635v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Learning reusable latent actions from action-free videos offers an effective route to improving Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies. However, reconstruction-oriented latent actions do not necessarily benefit policy learning: as they may encode task-irrelevant static appearance with scene identity, or entangle slowly varying task progress with fine-grained execution dynamics in limited discrete code. We propose FreshVLA, a VLA framework built on a frequency-guided, dynamics-sensitive learning paradigm for acquiring temporally hierarchical continuous latent actions. FreshVLA uses a high-pass prior to guide visual transition encoding toward dynamical regions, thereby reducing reliance on static appearance cues. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33705v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generating laboratory assets that faithfully reproduce the appearance, structure, and joint motions of real equipment remains challenging. Existing asset generation methods struggle to directly generate simulation assets for all equipment observed in operation videos and to faithfully reproduce the appearance, joint motions, and internal cavities of the real equipment. To address the challenge, we present Lab2Sim, an agentic framework that generates editable, simulation-ready laboratory equipment assets from egocentric or multi-view operation videos. Lab2Sim comprises four specialized agents. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33710v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation requires historical context, yet retaining extensive visual histories incurs growing storage and retrieval costs, while aggressive compression risks losing fine-grained information needed for subsequent decisions. Moreover, executed action histories capture intermediate behaviors that sparse visual observations may miss. Preserving this complementary context efficiently calls for modality-specific memory mechanisms that balance recent detail with long-term retention. To this end, we introduce $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM, a world-action model equipped with hierarchical visual and interaction memories. $\mathrm{M}^{2}$-WAM preserves recent visual observations in dense short-term memory while consolidating entries evicted from this window into fixed-size associative long-term memory through gated delta updates. articles.title: A general-purpose safe manipulator planning framework for diverse environments without retraining
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33721v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Nowadays, robots need to be retrained whenever their operating environment changes, and this prohibitive training cost keeps them far from daily use. The community is calling for innovations that bestow on a robot the ability to safely grasp different objects under different conditions without excessive training data and computing power. In response to this call, we present a general-purpose manipulator mission-planning framework, allowing a robot to safely perform manipulation tasks, such as grasping objects that fit in its gripper, across different operating environments without retraining its controllers. articles.title: Practice Makes Fluent: Learning to Use Earlier Predictions in Looped Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33722v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: People become faster at a task through practice, but models that improve with experience do not necessarily learn to use less computation. We train looped models, whose intermediate predictions allow earlier exits, to perform tasks with fewer iterations through practice. This is difficult because shared-weight updates can degrade the final-loop prediction while improving early ones, and the exit gate must track early predictions as their quality changes. We propose FLUENT, which requires no additional task labels or rewards: it distills the initial model's final-loop prediction into early predictions, anchors the current final-loop prediction to the same frozen teacher, and trains the exit gate to balance disagreement with the current final-loop prediction against computation cost. articles.title: RoboJackVR: Turning Robot Tasks into VR Games for Scalable Demonstration Collection
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33731v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Scaling robot demonstration datasets requires collection systems that accommodate more participants and diverse tasks, yet teleoperation barriers and task-adaptation effort limit this expansion. We present RoboJackVR, a standalone virtual reality (VR) game in which players manipulate simulated robots to execute combat skills and contribute demonstrations. MuJoCo simulation and demonstration recording run locally on the headset, removing the need for an external PC or simulation server during collection. Tutorials, skill selection, combat consequences, and character progression organize repeated task attempts within a continuing game. articles.title: PROVE: Predict-to-Specify and Observe-to-Verify for Human-Aligned Evaluation of Mobile Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33733v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Judging open-world robot manipulation is hard because layouts, articulated fixtures, and valid goal configurations vary widely. On RoboCasa365, simulator predicates agree with human judgments on only 69.09\% of rollouts, and a frontier VLM judge on 86.12\%. We present \textbf{PROVE} (Predict-to-Specify, Observe-to-Verify), which first specifies what success should look like and then checks the outcome. PROVE refines success conditions from the instruction, the initial scene, a target-object reference image, and a generated goal image. The goal image only sharpens the conditions and never serves as evidence. On 6,500 human-annotated rollouts over 65 atomic actions, PROVE reaches \textbf{96.83\%} agreement. Applied to open-source policies, it reports far lower success than native checks and changes their ranking. articles.title: RegHarness: Regulating What Code-as-Policy Agents Keep from Steps to Skills
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.33739v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Code-as-Policy agents generate, execute, and revise robot programs, but often lack explicit mechanisms to govern what persists across executions: which actions are retained within a trial and which code modifications carry over to subsequent runs. This leaves two critical aspects of agent behavior insufficiently controlled: step-level execution and cross-run adaptation. We present RegHarness, a two-level harness that governs both forms of persistence for the RATs agent team, without relying on a vision-language-action (VLA) policy or demonstrations. Within each trial, run-time governance evaluates each proposed step from a reset scene, replaying the committed steps, while a fixed-rule controller commits the step only when both RATs' verifier and a task-long LLM auditor approve it. articles.title: AnyCam: Anything Can Represent Camera for Video Generation
articles.content: Camera-controlled video generation re-renders a video along a target camera trajectory, yet moving the camera around an object, the most natural way to change the viewpoint of an object-centric scene, remains difficult. Existing methods condition either on camera parameters, which are scale-ambiguous in monocular video, or on explicit geometry such as warped point clouds or depth, which breaks down under large viewpoint changes. We present AnyCam, a method that represents the camera with an anchor object in the scene: we reconstruct it in 3D and render it along the target trajectory, a camera signal that is scale-aware, view-complete and easy to specify relative to the object. A video diffusion model transfers the content and dynamics of the source video to the new viewpoint. Its H-Concat layout aligns source and target frames in time, so the model can be distilled into AnyCam-AR, a streaming few-step generator for on-the-fly camera control. Both models are trained on paired videos with pixel-aligned anchor renderings from multi-camera videos and static-scene captures. Experiments on diverse datasets and trajectories show that AnyCam performs favorably against camera-controlled video generation and 3D reconstruction methods in camera control and visual quality.

articles.title: Tracking Any Point with Agentic Visual Reasoning
articles.content: A general-purpose Vision-Language Model (VLM) has surpassed expert vision models in many domains such as object detection and video recognition. However, point correspondence is known to be challenging for VLMs since it goes beyond object-level recognition: it requires pixel-level localization of the same physical surface point across observations, even when appearance changes or the point disappears and later reappears. In this paper, we introduce AgenTAP, a VLM-based agent that directly predicts point coordinates and visibility and actively reasons over videos. Starting from its own estimate, the agent autonomously chooses what to inspect and uses the resulting evidence to verify point identity and refine its predictions. With GPT-6 Astra, it surpasses expert vision models in both point localization and visibility prediction, without correspondence-specific fine-tuning. We further use AgenTAP to re-identify physical points after disappearance and reconnect fragmented tracks, constructing EgoTAP-4D, a dataset of 3D point trajectories in long real-world egocentric videos. On sampled reappearing points, its predictions approach human agreement, and adding EgoTAP-4D to D4RT training improves average 3D tracking performance.
